clue.text: Port served when nave has been refurbished

indicators.note: something refurbished is done up anew, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship's crew is waited on at table once the church nave has been done up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been refurbished' tells you to rearrange WHEN and NAVE together; 'served' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Newhaven is a ferry harbour town on the Sussex coast of England, so it is a port by example.

clue.text: Determined to acquire conifer by may 1st

parts.note: a fir is a cone-bearing evergreen tree

indicators.note: '1st' after a word asks for that word's opening letter only

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to buy a pine tree before the first of May.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and determined are synonyms for resolute, unwavering in purpose.

clue.text: Apprehensive about councillor writing a slogan

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so one word's synonym goes round the other's abbreviation

parts.note: apprehensive means wary, nervous

explanation.surface: A nervous local councillor drafts a catchy slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: A war cry is a rallying shout, and by extension any campaigning slogan.

clue.text: Ada being awful? No, just joking!

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone calls Ada's conduct awful, then hastily adds that it was only a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges ADA and BEING; 'No, just' are filler linking words in the surface's retraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light teasing banter, a form of playful humorous talk.

clue.text: As immature as can be, and showing the lack of a professional touch

definitions.text: showing the lack of a professional touch

indicators.note: the letters are shown as they can be when rearranged, a loose signal to reorder the words before it

explanation.surface: Being as childish as possible, someone does a job without any expert skill.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'as can be' acts on AS and IMMATURE together; the second 'as' belongs to the indicator, not the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurism is the non-expert quality of work done without trained skill, the opposite of a pro's polish.

clue.text: Usher in the prince's cortège

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning their join

explanation.surface: An attendant leads guests within a royal funeral procession.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher someone is to guide or accompany them, which is to escort them.

clue.text: Surprisingly the saint appeared irresolute

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected change, so the letters of the next two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Against expectations, the holy figure seemed unable to make up their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitant and irresolute both describe someone wavering, unable to decide.

clue.text: Time to fish for seaweed

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod and line

explanation.surface: It is time to go fishing for seaweed at the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangle is a name for kelp, a large brown seaweed of rocky coasts.

clue.text: Maureen's in a lieutenant's embrace — practically

indicators.note: an embrace holds something within it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, here with its possessive S
Mo is a short form of the name Maureen, here with its possessive S

explanation.surface: Maureen is nearly held in the arms of a junior army officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Both possessives keep their S: MOS goes inside LTS, all after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost and practically both mean very nearly, not quite.

clue.text: A caprice of western man

parts.note: him is the pronoun standing for a man

explanation.surface: A cowboy hero acts on a sudden fancy.
explanation.definitionFit: A whim is a sudden impulsive fancy, the same as a caprice.

clue.text: No doubt it follows proof of guilt

explanation.surface: Certainty arrives once a crime has been proved in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is firm belief or certainty; the second is the formal court verdict declaring a defendant guilty.

clue.text: Bird sanctuary by a Roman road beside a railway

parts.note: via is the Latin word for road, as in Via Appia

explanation.surface: A nature reserve for birds lies next to an ancient road and a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is a large enclosure where birds are kept safely, a haven for them.

clue.text: A governing body is trendy in the main

parts.note: a board is a committee that governs an organisation
is shortens to 's
hip means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: A fashionable committee meets for business on the main agenda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic word for the open sea, so 'in the main' means at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aboard a vessel puts you at sea, which the poetic 'main' names.

clue.text: Star performer competent enough to prepare in stages

parts.note: the lead is the principal actor in a show
up to a task means capable of it

explanation.surface: A leading actor is capable enough to rehearse step by step.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead up to something is to build gradually towards it, paving the way stage by stage.

clue.text: Idiot demands a bit of pasta

explanation.surface: A fool insists on getting a scrap of spaghetti.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is slang for a silly person (also the head); the second is a strip of dough such as a ribbon of tagliatelle.

clue.text: Freedom to display its lines on a map

explanation.surface: A cartographer enjoys the freedom to draw parallels across a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is scope or leeway to act; the second is angular distance north or south of the equator, shown by parallels on maps.

clue.text: Army men willingly provide welfare

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
lief is an old word meaning gladly or willingly, as in 'I'd as lief'

explanation.surface: Soldiers gladly hand out aid to the needy.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief is help given to those in need, which is what welfare provides.

clue.text: Dashes back to apartment in agitated state

parts.note: flat is the British word for an apartment

indicators.note: back means the word for dashes is read from end to start

parts.note: to nip is to dash or pop somewhere quickly

explanation.surface: Someone races home to their flat in a state of nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' tells you to read the dashes word from end to start; the reversed piece comes after the apartment even though the clue names it first.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat spin is a panicky, flustered condition, borrowed from an aircraft's uncontrolled spiral.

clue.text: Prior to race meeting, male displays charm

indicators.note: prior to means coming before, so one piece is placed ahead of the other

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse and its royal race meeting

explanation.surface: Before a day at the races, a man shows off his lucky talisman.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a racecourse in Berkshire, England, famous for its royal meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a lucky charm, an object thought to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Peter to produce a work of note

indicators.note: to produce is to make something new, so these letters are worked into another form

explanation.surface: Peter sets out to create a musical composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' rearranges PETER and TO into OPERETT; the A is added at the end as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a light opera, a musical piece, hence a work made of musical notes.

clue.text: Stop for a time

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a pause to last a while.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is the full-stop punctuation mark; the second is a span or era of history.

clue.text: Struggle to dress doctor in outdoor wear

indicators.note: to dress someone is to clothe them, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a coat is worn outdoors
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so stands for a doctor

explanation.surface: Someone wrestles to get a doctor into an overcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting, a physical contest or conflict.

clue.text: Street trader who must price his goods

explanation.surface: A barrow boy has to put a price on his wares.
explanation.walkthrough: A COSTER (costermonger) is a London street seller of fruit and vegetables; the second reading is whimsical, one who costs things.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a barrow seller of produce; the second jokingly treats the word as one who sets what items cost.

clue.text: Store put in money to provide basics

indicators.note: put in means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
a stack is a pile or store of things

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper banks cash to cover essential needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' is northern British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to brass tacks means dealing with fundamental matters, the essentials.

clue.text: Quite right

explanation.surface: A two-word agreement: entirely correct.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense means only or merely, as in 'just so'; the second means fair and morally proper.

clue.text: Judge gets pub to serve spirits

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A magistrate takes over a tavern to sell alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Jinn are supernatural beings of Arabic lore, genies, hence spirits.

clue.text: Wealthy Scotsman and I confront top journalist

parts.note: mon is a stereotyped Scots form of 'man'
ED, editor, is the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A Scotsman and I face down a newspaper's chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Monied (also moneyed) means rich, having plenty of cash.

clue.text: Made trainee get large dowel

indicators.note: made suggests something put together, so the next word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An apprentice is put to work to fetch a big wooden peg.
explanation.definitionFit: A treenail is a wooden peg used to fasten timbers, a kind of dowel.
